title: Arithmetic intensity vs batch size (main-memory traffic model)
caption: Packet-owned computation from the chapter's running network: FLOPs over bytes moved under a stream-everything model, I = 2B·109,184 / (4B·986 + 4·109,386). Batching reuses each weight read across examples, climbing the bandwidth slope from ~0.5 to ~12 at batch 32 — and past the ~20 ridge by batch 128, where the model overstates real traffic because runtimes keep weights resident between steps. Book confirms ~0.5 (B=1) and ~12 (B=32).

title: Training vs inference memory at batch 32 (KB, FP32)
caption: The four-state decomposition for the running network. Inference keeps weights plus the largest adjacent pair of activation buffers (~462 KB total); a training step adds gradients, one momentum-style optimizer copy, and all saved layer outputs (~1.3 MB, ~3x). Simplified single-device accounting matching the book's budget table; real runtimes add workspace and framework overhead.

title: MACs per layer: the first layer holds 91.9%
caption: Multiply-accumulates per digit by layer for 784-128-64-10. The input layer dominates because it meets the widest operand (784) at the widest matrix, 100,352 of 109,184 MACs. This is why input resolution is a cost axis, not just a fidelity axis: a 56x56 input would roughly quadruple the dominant term.
